subject: Troubles using predict() with occuMulti with four species and several covariates

messages.author: 931f5168d371d4cc
messages.subject: Troubles using predict() with occuMulti with four species and several covariates
parts:
Dear all,

I am new to this group and to the unmarked package so I apologize in advance if my question seems simple or doesn't make sense.

 I have some troubles using the predict function after using occuMulti to model the effect of several covariates on the occupancy of four species (R1, R2, R3 and R4), and on their respective detections.

 

1. I have trouble obtaining detection estimates using predict in a simple model with no covariates on occupancy:

 

The model is as follows:

# detection formula

det_formula_17 <- rep('~vegetation_det +RAI_human_log + progression',4) # for R1, R2, R3, R4 respectively

 

# occupancy model without interactions and no covariates

occ_formula_0 <- c('~1','~1','~1','~1', # first order f1,f2, f3, f4

                   '~0','~0', '~0','~'0,'~0','~0', #second order f12, f13, f14,f23,f24, f34 - two way interaction

                   '~0','~0','~0','~0', # third order f123, f124,f134, f234 - three way interactions

                   '~0' ) # fourth order f1234

 

 

fmdet_17 <- occuMulti(det_formula_17,

                      occ_formula_0,

                      data_df,

                      control = list(maxit = 3000, trace = 1))

 

#display  result

fmdet_17

 

#create a new data set use in predict

r <- range(data_df@siteCovs$RAI_human_log)

x <- seq(r[1], r[2], length.out = 100)

 

nd <-  data.frame( 

RAI_human_log = x,

vegetation_det =factor( "close", levels= c("close", "open")),

progression = factor("early", levels = c("early", "late")))

 

predict(fmdet_17, type = 'det', species = "R1", newdata = nd)

 

it kind of works if the argument ‘se.fit’ is set to FALSE, otherwise it gives the following error :  "Error in xb %*% t(x) %*% cov_sub : inadequate arguments" (sorry, I had to translate the last bit from French so it may not say exactly that).

 

2. I also have trouble using predict to obtain occupancy estimates while accounting for imperfect detection (using the formulae presented above)

 

My code is as follows for this second model:

 

#default detection formula - same as above

det_formula <- rep('~vegetation_det +RAI_human_log + progression',4) #For  R1, R2, R3, R4 respectively

 

# Occupancy model with no interactions

occ_formula_14 <- c( paste( rep("~water_distance + vegetation_occ", 4),c( "RAI_R1_log", "RAI_R2_log", "RAI_R3_log", "RAI_R4_log"),  sep = ' + '), # first order f1,f2, f3, f4 

                     '~0','~0', '~0','~0','~0','~0', # no  two way interactions

                     '~0','~0','~0','~0', # no three way interactions 

                     '~0' ) # no four way interaction

 

 

fm1_14 <- occuMulti(det_formula,

                    occ_formula_14,

                    data_df,

                    control = list(maxit = 3000, trace = 1))

 

#display  results

 

fm1_14

(summary(fm1_14))

 

# Create new water_distance data 

r <- range(data_df@siteCovs$water_distance)  

x <- seq( r[1], r[2], length.out = 100)

 

# create new data to use in predict

nd_occ_1 <- data.frame(

                       water_distance = x , 

                       # keep other covariates constant

                       vegetation_occ = factor("absence", levels = c("absence", "presence")), 

                       RAI_R1_log = 0,

                       RAI_R2_log = 0,

                       RAI_R3_log = 0,

                       RAI_R4_log = 0  ,

                       # detection covariates 

                       vegetation_det = factor("close", levels= c("close", "open")),

                       RAI_human_log = 0,

                       progression = factor("early", levels = c("early", "late")))

 

 

predict(fm1_14,  type ='state', species = 'R1', newdata = nd_occ_1 )

 

Some additional info on covariates :

vegetation_occ and vegetation_det: site-specific covariate, categorical

water_distance: site-specific covariate, continuous

RAI_R1_log  and RAI_human_log : site-specific covariate, continuous 

progression: observational covariate, categorical

effort: observational covariate, continuous

 

Since I only wanted the marginal occupancy, at first, I only included the occupancy covariates in my new dataset, but when I ran predict I kept having the following error :  "Error in eval(predvars, data, env) : object 'vegetation_det' not found"

 

However, when I added the detection covariates, that same error kept showing.

And it seems that there are no errors in the spelling of the column names. 


Does anyone have an idea where the problem might comes from ?

 

I hope this makes sense, please let me know if it doesn’t, or if you need more details.

Also, I am sorry for the length of this message.

 

I thank you in advance for your help or any advice you may have,

 

Best regards,

Aïssa Morin

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: Troubles using predict() with occuMulti with four species and several covariates
parts:
Hi Aïssa,

The predict function for occuMulti has some bugs for which the fixes haven't made it to CRAN yet. It looks like you are running in to at least one or more of those bugs, sorry. Can you try installing the development version of the unmarked to see if that fixes some or all of your problems?

One way to install it would be to use the install_github() function in the devtools package:

library(devtools)
install_github("rbchan/unmarked")

Then restart R and load unmarked, and try your code again. On Windows you will also need Rtools (https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/) also installed to use this method.

If that doesn't work for you and you are using Windows, email me off-list and I can send you the development version that way.

Ken
